quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: An intersection.
A road curve.
A right turn.
A lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done enough.
You must wait for the police to arrive.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A red light is ahead.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
A green light is ahead.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a traffic signal at the next intersection.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?

options.text: A railroad crossing is ahead.
A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. You can only cross these lines to turn left or pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Move to the right lane.
Stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go only when it is safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing before crossing.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a snowplow that is working?

options.text: Treat it like any other vehicle.
Assume they will let you go first.
Give them the right-of-way and be careful.
Stop completely until it is out of sight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give them the right-of-way and be careful.
questions.explanation: Always give snowplows the right-of-way. Be extra careful around them because they are large and create clouds of snow that can hide the plow from view.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with a bicyclist ahead going the same direction. How should you pass safely?

options.text: Slow down, wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
Keep driving straight. The bicyclist should move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like you would any other vehicle, but carefully. Leave at least 3 feet of space on regular roads, or 5 feet on faster roads or with groups of cyclists. Do not honk suddenly as it may scare them.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Passing bad drivers to stay ahead in traffic.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you recognize dangerous situations before they happen and take action to stay safe. It helps you avoid accidents caused by careless, aggressive, or distracted drivers.

questions.question: What do some highways use to guide drivers into the correct turn lanes?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows painted in the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted in the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows on the road show which lanes to use for turning or going straight.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Let pedestrians go first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go, but only after you let pedestrians and other traffic still in the intersection pass first.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street. This is true even if they cross against the red light or are being careless.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment depends on:

options.text: Whether you drink beer instead of wine.
Whether you drink wine instead of beer.
Whether you drink hard ciders and mixed drinks.
How much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol is in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road ahead has curves or turns.
Traffic will increase ahead.
A steep hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Slow down, avoid sudden braking or sharp turns, and stay farther back from the car ahead.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
The same thing as a yellow circular traffic light.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.
A green arrow will appear soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a yellow circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a yellow light. Slow down and get ready to stop when the light turns red.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to find a chance to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. Bicyclists have little protection. Passing too close or too fast can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how quickly you can stop. Slow down on slippery or poor roads. Driving too fast on bad roads puts you at risk.

questions.question: As you near an intersection, the traffic light turns yellow. Your best action is to:

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop quickly.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Be ready to stop safely before you enter the intersection.

questions.question: A flashing red light on a traffic signal means:

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: The best way to deal with tailgaters is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see if someone is following too close or trying to pass. Slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When you want to make a right turn, where should your car be?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road before you turn right. Do not cross other lanes of traffic to make your turn.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate at a railroad crossing that is moving up or down?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not close.
Yes, if your vehicle fits under it.
Yes, if you look both ways first.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing red lights, lowered gates, or bells at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: Where should you never make a U-turn?

options.text: At the top of a hill.
Near a curve.
Where you cannot see 500 feet ahead in both directions.
Any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not make a U-turn at the top of a hill, near a curve, or anywhere you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Only make a U-turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A blind spot around a truck or bus where you cannot be seen.
A special speed zone.
An area with rules about stereo volume.
A television show.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blind spot around a truck or bus where you cannot be seen.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Cars in these spots cannot be seen. These areas are called "No zones."

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up or slow down so the driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so they can see you.
